New runs: the read gain at 8 MiB by size, history and time

TEST DATA: stand-in kernels or shortened durations; no decision

Short version. This page is built from test data: the kernels are stand-ins or the durations were shortened, so the rates mean nothing and no decision is given. The folders hold 608 processes and 5736 trials of the steps B6W, BIN, C4, CM, CS, P3, P3G, S2, S3, S3G, S4: 0 trials are rejected, 1132 carry a disturbed mark, and 0 processes did not end.

Words used here

  • 8 MiB: 8,388,608 bytes. This is the buffer size called "8 MB" in the question.
  • Rate: bytes read divided by measured elapsed time, in GB/s. One GB is 1,000,000,000 bytes.
  • Old read, new read, assembly read: the read loops before the rewrite, after the rewrite, and written in assembly. Their names in the program are oldread, read and asmread. New read and assembly read are the load-only kernels.
  • Kernel: one of these benchmark loops. It is not the Linux kernel.
  • CRB: the Arm Phoenix Reference Server where the measurements run.
  • bwx8: the benchmark program of this design. run_bwx8.sh starts its processes. analyze8 is the analysis program that computes every number and decision of this page.
  • Process: one start of bwx8. It has one fresh buffer (one allocation).
  • Session: one complete set of processes. Session 2 starts at least 3 hours after session 1 ends.
  • Trial: prefix, optional predecessor, and target, in that order, on one buffer and one CPU.
  • Prefix: the same preparation loop before each trial. It is not assumed to reset the hardware.
  • Predecessor: the loop deliberately run immediately before the loop being measured.
  • Target: the loop whose subsequent rate is measured.
  • Window: one measured period inside the prefix or target. The target has four windows. The fourth window is the primary value. The first window is shown beside it.
  • Process rate: the median of the window rate over the four trials (repeats) of one condition in one process.
  • Matched set: in Stage 2, the three processes (one per kernel) with the same replicate number, size, CPU and session. A CPU and session has six sets.
  • Unit: the thing counted six times per CPU and session: a matched set in Stage 2, one process elsewhere.
  • Gain: 100 × (new / old − 1), in percent.
  • A/A value: median(repeat 1, repeat 3) − median(repeat 2, repeat 4) of one process, condition and window. Both halves ran the same condition.
  • A/A spread: the largest absolute A/A value over the six processes of one CPU and session.
  • Limit: the sum of the A/A spreads of the rates in a contrast. It measures variation inside processes only.
  • Repeatable: the word for a contrast on one CPU and session whose median over the six units is above the limit in absolute value, with six values of one sign.
  • Confirmed: repeatable in both sessions with the same sign on a CPU.
  • P1: prediction 1: old read stays nearly constant from 1 MiB to 8 MiB. Equivalent means that every one of the six |difference| + limit values is at most 0.30 GB/s.
  • P2: prediction 2: the load-only kernels lose rate from 1 MiB to 8 MiB.
  • P3: prediction 3: old read stays stable across the variation of the load-only rate at 8 MiB, on one allocation.
  • ΔG: the lost advantage, (new at 1 MiB − new at 8 MiB) − (old at 1 MiB − old at 8 MiB), in GB/s. Its two brackets are the new-read term and the old-read term.
  • Gate: an acceptance check. It passes on a CPU and session only if |median difference| is at most the limit, the limit is below the margin, and |median difference| + limit is at most the margin.
  • Margin: the largest difference that a gate may overlook, frozen in a file before the gate batch ran.
  • Filtered, unfiltered: filtered leaves out trials with a disturbed mark or a coverage mark. Unfiltered keeps every trial with valid accounting. Decisions use the filtered estimate.
  • Rejected: a trial left out of every estimate: interrupted, or its accounting or required records failed.
  • Disturbed: a mark on a trial: thread CPU time below 99 % of the wall time, an involuntary context switch, or a gap above 100 µs before the target.
  • Coverage change: a mark on a trial whose huge-page coverage (the part of the buffer on 2 MiB pages) differs between its two page readings.
  • Steps: B6W: replay of the earlier B6 sequence. S2: Stage 2, one kernel and size per process. S4: Stage 4, 60 s of one kernel. P3G and S3G: prefix gates. P3: three kernels on one allocation. S3: Stage 3, mixed sequences. BIN: 10 ms bins against window records. CS, CM, C4: runs with counters.
  • Counter: a hardware event count for the worker thread.
  • System load: the 1 minute load average of Linux (mean number of runnable tasks), read directly before each process starts.
  • est.: an estimate, not a measurement.

1. What this page is built from

  • The page reports new runs of the design "explain the small read-bandwidth gain at 8 MiB" [Ref1].
  • The analysis program computed every number of a rule and every decision word [Ref3]. This page only draws them.
  • The result folders are listed in the references [Ref4].
  • A dash (–) in a table means that the analysis has no value there. The count columns and the exclusion table show why.

3. Stage 2: old read against new read by buffer size

Each process ran one kernel at one size: a 1.2 s prefix of that kernel, then four target windows of 0.3 s, four times [Ref1] [Ref2]. The charts show the fourth window. The first window is shown as rings below it.

old read (median of the processes)new readassembly readfirst-window median, same coloursold-to-new gap

CPU 2, session 1

Under preparation "same-kernel prefix asmread@8M for 8 ms / oldread@8M for 8 ms / read@8M for 8 ms" on CPU 2 in session 1, old read was 161.60 GB/s and new read was 39.99 GB/s at 8 MiB (medians of 2 and 3 processes). The gain was -74.79 % (median of 1 matched sets, range -74.79 to -74.79 %).

All sizes on one axis from 0. Small faint dots are the six process rates. The labels at the right give the gain of new read over old read: the median of the matched sets, their range, and the first-window median.

The same data at 8 MiB and 16 MiB only, on a narrow axis. It shows whether the load-only rates approach or cross the old-read rate.

P1: is old read nearly constant from 1 MiB to 8 MiB?

Rule: d is old read at 8 MiB minus old read at 1 MiB in one matched set, fourth window. L is the limit (two A/A spreads). P1 is "equivalent" on a CPU and session only if every one of the six |d| + L values is at most 0.30 GB/s. It is "contradicted" if the contrast is repeatable and its median is above 0.30 GB/s in absolute value. Otherwise it is "undecided" [Ref1] [Ref2].

One dot per matched set. The dashed line is the margin of P1.

P2: do the load-only kernels lose rate from 1 MiB to 8 MiB?

5. P3: old read against the load-only kernels on one allocation

Each process ran old read, new read and assembly read on one 8 MiB allocation, each with its own 1.2 s prefix, four times [Ref1]. This is a relation across preparations on the same allocation. It is not proof that a hidden state persisted while the kernels changed.

Rules, per CPU and session and per selecting kernel X (new read, then assembly read): without a passed prefix gate P3G the result is "Insufficient data". A process is unstable if its four fourth-window rates span more than 0.30 GB/s or a trial has |first − fourth window| above 0.30 GB/s: then "Insufficient data". A range of the six X medians below 2.0 GB/s: "Insufficient data". Control limit = 2 × the largest |A/A value| of old read. "compatible" if the old-read range plus the control limit is at most 0.30 GB/s. "contrary" if |old at the process of highest X − old at the process of lowest X| minus the control limit is above 0.30 GB/s. Otherwise "undecided" [Ref2].

Prefix gate P3G passed: no decision (not evaluated, or test data).

x = new-read rate of the processx = assembly-read rate of the processprocess with an instability mark

The endpoints are selected observations, not six confirmed interventions. A state dependence needs a new controlled batch before a mechanism is assigned.

6. Stage 3: does the predecessor change the next measurement?

Every trial ran the common old-read prefix (1.2 s), one predecessor (0.3 s), then the target in four windows of 0.3 s [Ref1] [Ref2]. The panels show the target rate against the actual time since the end of the predecessor.

after old read at 8 MiBafter new read at 8 MiBafter assembly read at 8 MiBafter old read on the first 1 MiB

CPU 17, session 2

Rate in GB/s. Thin lines: every trial with valid accounting. Thick lines: the median of those trials in each window, at the median of the actual window centres. The y axis does not start at 0.

Primary contrasts with their limits

Rule: a contrast is "repeatable" on a CPU and session if its median over the six processes is outside the grey band (± the limit) and all six values have one sign. The first window is the primary test of immediate history. The fourth window is the persistence check [Ref1].

CPU 2, session 2

CPU 17, session 2

One dot per process. Black tick: median. Grey band: from −limit to +limit. A negative value in the first two rows means that old read is slower after that predecessor than after old read.

7. Gates: acceptance checks before a conclusion may use a prefix or a measurement mode

Rule: a gate contrast is the difference inside a process between two previous activities or two measurement modes. It gets the word "pass" on a CPU and session only if |median| is at most the limit, the limit is below the frozen margin, and |median| + limit is at most the margin. "precision insufficient": the limit is at or above the margin, or the median is inside the limit but |median| + limit is above the margin. "resolved difference": the contrast is repeatable. "not established": the rest. Every contrast of a use must pass on both CPUs in both sessions [Ref1] [Ref2].

The margins come from the frozen file of the forecast command [Ref5].

8. B6W: replay of the earlier B6 sequence

Each process replayed the 13-entry sequence of the earlier experiment B6 for four rounds with the unchanged interval wrapper [Ref1] [Ref2]. It holds 8 pairs of consecutive old-read intervals directly after assembly read.

Rule: the positional effect is "reproduced" on a CPU and session only if the first interval is slower in all 8 pairs in both processes. This check is descriptive and exempt from the six-process rule.

One dot per pair. A dot left of 0 means that the first old-read interval after assembly read was the slower one.

12. What explains what

The table follows the design section "What counts as progress, and what counts as an answer" [Ref1]. A conclusion is printed only where the analysis returned the evidence of its row. This page adds no causal sentence of its own.

result named by the designevidence in these runsallowed conclusion, or what is missing
Reproduced low and high rates36 sustained traces; 36 of them have a step above 0.30 GB/s between successive windows (section 4).Insufficient data. The analysis returns no decision that a low and a high rate were reproduced. The lines at 69 and 70.5 GB/s are annotations only. Next measurement: a controlled intervention that changes a listed transition, chosen under Stage 5 of the design.

Test data gives no decision. Next measurement: the Stage 3 batch with six complete processes per CPU in both sessions.
Confirmed change of the old-to-new gain in a mixed sequenceContrast "(new − old) after new read − (new − old) after old read", first window. Confirmed per CPU: CPU 2 no decision, CPU 17 no decision. On both CPUs with one sign: no decision. CPU 2, session 1: median – GB/s, limit 16.97 GB/s; CPU 2, session 2: median – GB/s, limit 20.16 GB/s; CPU 17, session 1: median −1.48 GB/s, limit 28.80 GB/s; CPU 17, session 2: median +5.76 GB/s, limit 15.27 GB/s.Insufficient data. The 8 MiB question is not solved because one hypothesis is not rejected. A complete answer needs the old and new rates under controlled conditions, the part of the gap explained by an intervention, and the remaining uncertainty [Ref1].
